Novhorodka Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Novhorodka, Ukraine

Demolished. Novhorodka (originally Kutsovka), settled by Cossacks in 1768 and later part of the Kherson Governorate, was officially renamed in 1822 and became a shtetl by 1860; a Jewish prayer house opened in 1886. The Jewish population was always a small minority - just a few dozen among 8,230 total residents by 1897. The community endured Soviet repression, the Holodomor famine, and the Holocaust alongside their neighbors. The cemetery is now demolished and built over, though a 1941 map shows an unclear marking suggesting a Jewish cemetery once stood at this location.
